questions.question: Consider the network diagram. What is the sum of the degrees of all the vertices in this network?
questions.answer: Degrees: $A=2$, $B=4$ (including the curved edge to $C$), $C=3$, $D=3$, $E=2$. Sum $=14$, which is twice the 7 edges (D).

questions.question: A new mountain bike was purchased for \$1386, including 10% GST. What was the price of the bike before GST, correct to the nearest dollar?
questions.answer: The price including GST is $110\%$ of the original price: $1386\div1.1=\$1260$ (B).

questions.question: Most cars use fuel that is a blend of 90% petrol and 10% ethanol. What is the ratio of petrol to ethanol in this blend?
Consider the line below. What is the equation of the line?
questions.answer: The $y$-intercept is 4 and the line falls 2 units for every 1 unit to the right (through $(2,0)$), so the gradient is $-2$: $y=-2x+4$ (D).

questions.question: What is the correct expression for the value of $x$ in this triangle?
questions.answer: The side of length 4 is adjacent to the $65^\circ$ angle and $x$ is the hypotenuse, so $\cos65^\circ=\dfrac4x$ and $x=\dfrac{4}{\cos65^\circ}$ (A).

questions.question: Young's formula is used to calculate the required dosages of medicine for children aged 1–12 years: $\text{Dosage}=\dfrac{\text{age of child (in years)}\times\text{adult dosage}}{\text{age of child (in years)}+12}$. The adult dosage is 45 mL. How much medicine should be given to an 18-month-old child in a 24-hour period if the child has a dose of medicine every 6 hours?
questions.answer: Age $=1.5$ years: dose $=\dfrac{1.5\times45}{1.5+12}=5$ mL. There are $24\div6=4$ doses in 24 hours, so the total is $4\times5=20$ mL (B).

questions.question: A table of future value interest factors for an annuity of \$1 is shown. Peta made equal contributions of \$2500 into an account at the end of every 6 months for 2 years at an interest rate of 4% per annum. What is the future value of this annuity?
questions.answer: There are $4$ periods and the rate is $2\%$ per period, so the factor is $4.1216$. $FV=2500\times4.1216=\$10\,304.00$ (A).

questions.question: The costs of two mobile phone plans are Plan A: $y=0.1x+15$ and Plan B: $y=0.2x+10$, where $y$ is the total monthly cost in dollars and $x$ is the number of call minutes used. The equations are graphed on the same axes below. At what number of call minutes do both plans cost the same?
questions.answer: The lines intersect at $x=50$ (algebraically $0.1x+15=0.2x+10\Rightarrow x=50$), where both plans cost \$20 (D).

questions.question: A map has a scale of 1:20 000. Two towns are 12 km apart in real life. How far apart are the two towns on the map, in centimetres?
The daily production costs and revenue from the sale of a particular item are shown on the graph. Which statement is incorrect?
questions.answer: The lines intersect at 5 items (\$10), the break-even point, so no profit is made at 5 items and statement C is incorrect. At 10 items revenue is \$20 and cost is \$15 (profit \$5), and at 15 items revenue is \$30 and cost is \$20 (profit \$10).
options: If 5 items are sold, no profit is made.
If 10 items are sold a profit of \$5 is made.
If 5 items are sold, a profit of \$10 is made.
If 15 items are sold a profit of \$10 is made.

questions.question: A factory has a large juice tank that holds 16 kL of freshly squeezed orange juice. If each bottle holds 750 mL, approximately how many bottles can be filled?
The diagram shows a radial survey of a field $ABCD$. What is the distance between $A$ and $B$, correct to the nearest metre?
questions.answer: $A$ is on a bearing of $308^\circ$ and $B$ on $060^\circ$ from $O$, so $\angle AOB=360^\circ-308^\circ+60^\circ=112^\circ$. By the cosine rule $AB^2=100^2+30^2-2(100)(30)\cos112^\circ\approx13\,147.6$, so $AB\approx114.7\approx115$ m (B).

questions.question: A coin is biased so it shows heads to tails in the ratio of 2:3 when it is tossed. Find the number of heads expected if the coin is tossed 100 times.
questions.answer: $P(\text{head})=\dfrac25$, so the expected number of heads is $\dfrac25\times100=40$ (B).

questions.question: Two identical spheres fit exactly inside a cylindrical container, as shown. The diameter of each sphere is 10 cm. What is the volume of the cylindrical container, to the nearest cubic centimetre?
questions.answer: The cylinder has radius 5 cm and height $2\times10=20$ cm: $V=\pi r^2h=\pi(5)^2(20)\approx1571$ cm$^3$ (B).

questions.question: A random variable is normally distributed with a mean of 0 and a standard deviation of 1. The probability that this random variable lies below $a$, for some positive value of $a$, is represented by the shaded area. Which of the following statements is false?
questions.answer: By symmetry $P(z<-a)=P(z>a)$ (A) and $P(z>-a)=P(z<a)=1-P(z>a)$ (B). The central area is $P(z<a)-P(z<-a)=P(z<a)-(1-P(z<a))=2P(z<a)-1$ (C is true), so D, which has the opposite sign, is false. For example if $P(z<a)=0.9$ then $P(-a<z<a)=0.8$, but $1-2(0.9)=-0.8$.

questions.question: The number of points per game scored by a basketball team in a season is normally distributed with a mean of 116 points per game and a standard deviation of 2. What percentage of games will have between 112 and 118 points scored?
questions.answer: $112$ is 2 standard deviations below the mean ($z=-2$) and $118$ is 1 standard deviation above the mean ($z=1$). By the empirical rule, $\dfrac12(95\%)+\dfrac12(68\%)=47.5\%+34\%=81.5\%$.

questions.question: Solve $2x=\dfrac{x}{2}+6$.
questions.answer: Multiply both sides by 2: $4x=x+12$, so $3x=12$ and $x=4$.

questions.question: Use the trapezoidal rule to approximate the shaded area on the diagram (the parallel sides are 12 m and 8 m, and the distance between them is 8 m).
questions.answer: $A\approx\dfrac h2(d_f+d_l)=\dfrac82(12+8)=80\text{ m}^2$.

questions.question: Express 0.0009028 in scientific (standard) form. Give your answer correct to three significant figures.
Mona's heart beats 72 times per minute. How many times will it beat in 24 hours?
questions.answer: $72\times60\times24=103\,680$ beats.

questions.question: Make $y$ the subject of the equation $a=\sqrt{by-1}$.
questions.answer: Square both sides: $a^2=by-1$, so $by=a^2+1$ and $y=\dfrac{a^2+1}{b}$.

questions.question: Ray owns 1800 shares in a company. The total market price for the portfolio is \$27 000. Ray's dividend for each share is \$1.20. Calculate the dividend yield for his shares.
questions.answer: Share price $=\dfrac{27\,000}{1800}=\$15$. Dividend yield $=\dfrac{1.20}{15}=0.08=8\%$.

questions.question:
Jack and Judy are planning a fund-raising dance. They hire a hall for \$400 and a band for \$300. Refreshments will cost \$12 per person. The graph shows planned income and cost with the ticket price set at \$20 per person.

Write a formula for the cost (\$$C$) of running the dance for $x$ people.
questions.answer: Fixed costs are $400+300=\$700$ and refreshments are \$12 per person: $C=12x+700$.

questions.question:
Jack and Judy are planning a fund-raising dance. They hire a hall for \$400 and a band for \$300. Refreshments will cost \$12 per person. The graph shows planned income and cost with the ticket price set at \$20 per person.

Estimate the minimum number of people needed at the dance to cover the cost.
questions.answer: The income and cost lines intersect at about 88 people (the school's answer: about 90). Algebraically $20x=12x+700$ gives $x=87.5$, so at least 88 people are needed.

questions.question:
Jack and Judy are planning a fund-raising dance. They hire a hall for \$400 and a band for \$300. Refreshments will cost \$12 per person. The graph shows planned income and cost with the ticket price set at \$20 per person.

How much profit will be made if 150 people attend the dance?

Jack and Judy hire a hall for \$400 and a band for \$300, and refreshments cost \$12 per person. They plan to sell 200 tickets and want to make a profit of \$1500. What should be the price of a ticket, assuming all 200 tickets will be sold?
questions.answer: Cost for 200 people $=12(200)+700=\$3100$. Let the ticket price be $p$: income $=200p$. Profit $=$ income $-$ cost, so $1500=200p-3100$, giving $200p=4600$ and $p=\$23$.

questions.question: A bag contains 7 red balls and 13 blue balls. Two balls are selected at random without replacement. Draw a probability tree and calculate the probability of selecting two balls of the same colour.
questions.answer:
First draw: $P(R)=\dfrac7{20}$, $P(B)=\dfrac{13}{20}$. Second draw (no replacement): after a red, $P(R)=\dfrac6{19}$ and $P(B)=\dfrac{13}{19}$; after a blue, $P(R)=\dfrac7{19}$ and $P(B)=\dfrac{12}{19}$.

$P(\text{same colour})=P(RR)+P(BB)=\dfrac7{20}\times\dfrac6{19}+\dfrac{13}{20}\times\dfrac{12}{19}=\dfrac{42+156}{380}=\dfrac{99}{190}$.

questions.question: The school librarian records the reasons students visited the help desk during Term 1: Research Help 24 (cumulative frequency 24, cumulative percentage 48); Wifi Issues A (cumulative frequency 28, 56%); Find Book 12 (cumulative frequency 40, 80%); Printing Issues 5 (cumulative frequency B, 90%); New Card 3 (cumulative frequency 48, 99%); Forgotten Password 2 (cumulative frequency 50, 100%). The total is 50. What are the values of $A$ and $B$?
The box plot for a dataset is given. Is 10 an outlier? Justify your answer with calculations.
questions.answer: From the box plot $Q_1=3$ and $Q_3=7$, so $\text{IQR}=7-3=4$. The upper fence is $Q_3+1.5\times\text{IQR}=7+1.5\times4=13$. Since $10<13$, 10 is not an outlier.

questions.question: Charles's taxable income is \$88 225. Tax payable: \$0–\$18 200 nil; \$18 201–\$45 000: 16c for each \$1 over \$18 200; \$45 001–\$135 000: \$4288 plus 30c for each \$1 over \$45 000; \$135 001–\$190 000: \$31 288 plus 37c for each \$1 over \$135 000; \$190 001 and over: \$51 638 plus 45c for each \$1 over \$190 000. In addition he pays the Medicare levy, which is 2% of his taxable income. Calculate Charles's total tax payable.

The heights and weights of 8 preschoolers: heights $h$ (cm) 102, 100, 105, 98, 104, 99, 103, 101 with weights $w$ (kg) 16.5, 15.2, 17.8, 14.6, 17.2, 15, 16.1, 15.6 respectively.

Calculate the correlation coefficient, $r$. Give your answer correct to three significant figures.
questions.answer: Using a calculator's statistics mode: $r=0.9678\ldots\approx0.968$.

questions.question:
The heights and weights of 8 preschoolers: heights $h$ (cm) 102, 100, 105, 98, 104, 99, 103, 101 with weights $w$ (kg) 16.5, 15.2, 17.8, 14.6, 17.2, 15, 16.1, 15.6 respectively. The correlation coefficient is $r=0.968$.

Comment on the strength of the correlation.
questions.answer: $r=0.968$ is close to $+1$, so there is a very strong positive linear correlation between height and weight.

questions.question:
The heights and weights of 8 preschoolers: heights $h$ (cm) 102, 100, 105, 98, 104, 99, 103, 101 with weights $w$ (kg) 16.5, 15.2, 17.8, 14.6, 17.2, 15, 16.1, 15.6 respectively.

Find the equation of the least-squares regression line. Give the values in the equation correct to two decimal places.
questions.answer: From the calculator, the gradient is $0.4405\ldots\approx0.44$ and the intercept is $-28.7083\ldots\approx-28.71$, so $w=-28.71+0.44h$.

questions.question: The least-squares regression line for the heights ($h$ cm) and weights ($w$ kg) of preschoolers is $w=-28.71+0.44h$. Predict the weight of a preschooler who is 108 cm tall.
questions.answer: $w=-28.71+0.44(108)=18.81$ kg, so about 18.8 kg (using the unrounded line, 18.86 kg). Note that 108 cm is above the data range, so this is an extrapolation.

questions.question: Robert is buying a new car with a sale price of \$22 850. Stamp duty is calculated at \$3 for every \$100, or part thereof, of the sale price. Calculate the stamp duty payable.
questions.answer: $22\,850\div100=228.5$, so there are 229 lots of \$100 (including the part). Stamp duty $=229\times3=\$687$.

questions.question: Robert buys a new car for \$22 850. The total purchase costs include a \$79 registration fee, a \$55 number plate fee, stamp duty of \$687 and vehicle tax. Vehicle tax is based on the tare weight of the vehicle. The car has a tare weight of 1250 kg and is for private use. The private use fee is: up to 975 kg \$266; 976–1154 kg \$308; 1155–1504 kg \$374; 1505–2504 kg \$570; 2505–2794 kg \$822. Calculate the total amount Robert pays.
questions.answer: A tare weight of 1250 kg is in the 1155–1504 kg band, so the vehicle tax is \$374. Fees $=79+55+687+374=\$1195$. Total $=22\,850+1195=\$24\,045$.

questions.question: Robert has decided he will take out comprehensive car insurance in addition to the compulsory third party insurance. State ONE extra cover that is provided by the comprehensive car insurance.
questions.answer: Comprehensive insurance covers damage to Robert's own car (e.g. from an accident, theft, fire or storm); third-party insurance covers only injury to other people.

questions.question:
Jo has signed up for a premium gym membership. The upfront cost is \$3600, but the gym offers a payment plan allowing members to pay in equal quarterly instalments over 2 years, with an annual interest rate of 8% p.a. compounded quarterly. Present value interest factors for an annuity of \$1 include: 2% per period, 8 periods: 7.3255.

Find the value of each quarterly instalment Jo needs to make.
questions.answer: There are $N=8$ quarterly payments at $r=\dfrac8{4}=2\%$ per quarter, so the present value factor is 7.3255. $PV=\text{payment}\times\text{factor}$, so the payment $=\dfrac{3600}{7.3255}=\$491.43$.

questions.question: Jo pays 8 equal quarterly instalments of \$491.43. Find the total amount he will repay over the 2 years.
Jo's gym membership costs \$3600 upfront, or 8 quarterly instalments totalling \$3931.44. Find the total interest paid over the life of the payment plan.
Sue lives in New York ($40^\circ$ N, $74^\circ$ W). She plans to travel to Copenhagen, which is $15^\circ$ north and $86^\circ$ east of New York. What is the latitude and longitude of Copenhagen?
questions.answer: Latitude $=40^\circ+15^\circ=55^\circ$ N. Longitude: moving $86^\circ$ east from $74^\circ$ W gives $86-74=12^\circ$ E. Copenhagen is $55^\circ$ N, $12^\circ$ E.

questions.question: Copenhagen is in UTC+2 and New York is in UTC$-5$. Sue's plane leaves New York at 6:00 pm on Friday local time and flies non-stop to Copenhagen. The flight takes 9 hours and 50 minutes. What time and day is it in Copenhagen when the plane lands?
questions.answer: Copenhagen is $2-(-5)=7$ hours ahead of New York. Departure is 6:00 pm Friday in New York $=$ 1:00 am Saturday in Copenhagen. Adding the flight time of 9 h 50 min gives 10:50 am Saturday in Copenhagen.

questions.question:
A logistics company manages deliveries between a group of towns using one-way roads. The distances (km) are: Mapleton (M) to Brookvale (B) 8; M to Clearwater (C) 20; B to C 10; B to Riverton (R) 15; C to R 8; C to Stonebridge (S) 25; R to S 16.

Draw a weighted directed network diagram to represent the information.
questions.answer: The network has five vertices (M, B, C, R, S) and seven directed, weighted edges, one for each row of the table, as shown in the diagram.

questions.question: A logistics company manages deliveries between a group of towns using one-way roads. The distances (km) are: Mapleton (M) to Brookvale (B) 8; M to Clearwater (C) 20; B to C 10; B to Riverton (R) 15; C to R 8; C to Stonebridge (S) 25; R to S 16. A delivery needs to be made from Mapleton to Stonebridge and charges \$2.30 per km travelled. What is the lowest price the company could charge for this delivery?
questions.answer: Paths from M to S: M–B–R–S $=8+15+16=39$ km; M–B–C–S $=8+10+25=43$ km; M–B–C–R–S $=8+10+8+16=42$ km; M–C–R–S $=20+8+16=44$ km; M–C–S $=20+25=45$ km. The shortest path is M–B–R–S, 39 km. Lowest price $=39\times2.30=\$89.70$.

questions.question: The average daily step count of CodeNest staff is 8000 steps, with a standard deviation of 1200 steps. On a particular day, Oliver recorded 5600 steps. Calculate Oliver's $z$-score.

CodeNest has 280 employees, with an average daily step count of 8000 steps and a standard deviation of 1200 steps. Assuming the step counts are normally distributed, approximately how many employees recorded a higher step count than Oliver (5600 steps, $z=-2$) on that day?
questions.answer: By the empirical rule, $P(z<-2)\approx2.5\%$, so $P(z>-2)\approx50\%+47.5\%=97.5\%$. Number $\approx0.975\times280=273$ employees.

questions.question: Claudia has a credit card which has an interest rate of 16% per annum. The interest is compounded daily and is charged on the amount owing with no interest-free period. The period for which interest is charged includes the date of purchase and the date of payment. On 10th March, Claudia purchased tickets for \$620 using her credit card. No other purchases were made using this card for the remainder of the month. What amount was paid when the account was paid in full on 5th April?
questions.answer: Daily rate $=\dfrac{16\%}{365}=\dfrac{0.16}{365}$. Days from 10 March to 5 April inclusive: $22$ (10–31 March) $+5=27$ days. $FV=620\left(1+\dfrac{0.16}{365}\right)^{27}=\$627.38$.

questions.question: A random variable is normally distributed with mean 0 and standard deviation 1. The table gives the probability that this random variable lies below $z$. A manufacturer produces luxury scented candles. The mass of wax in each candle is normally distributed with a mean of 300 grams and a standard deviation of 4 grams. What percentage of candles would you expect to contain more than 302 grams of wax?
questions.answer: $z=\dfrac{302-300}{4}=0.5$. From the table $P(z<0.5)=0.691$, so $P(z>0.5)=1-0.691=0.309$. About 30.9% of candles contain more than 302 g.

questions.question: An outdoor adventurer uses a pedal-powered generator to recharge the battery of her satellite communication device while camping off-grid. While pedalling she burns energy at a rate of 720 kilocalories per hour. The generator converts this energy and stores it as electricity in the device's battery. Her device requires 1.8 kWh of electricity per day. How long must she pedal each day to generate enough energy to power the device? Give your answer in hours and minutes, correct to the nearest minute. (1 kcal = 4.184 kJ and 3600 kJ = 1 kWh.)
questions.answer: Energy needed $=1.8\times3600=6480$ kJ. Energy produced per hour $=720\times4.184=3012.48$ kJ. Time $=\dfrac{6480}{3012.48}=2.151$ h $=2$ h $9$ min (to the nearest minute).

questions.question:
The drama department at a school is planning a school musical. Activities (duration in weeks; predecessors): A Write script (5; none); B Audition cast (2; A); C Design set and costumes (4; A); D Cast rehearsals (6; B); E Build set and create costumes (3; C); F Rehearse with full staging (4; D, E); G Technical setup (1; E); H Final dress rehearsal (1; F, G).

Complete the network diagram for the school musical production (part of it is drawn).
questions.answer: Activity D ends at the node where F begins. E ends at the node where G begins. F needs both D and E, so a dummy activity (dashed) joins the end of E to the start of F. F and G both lead to the node where H begins.

questions.question:
The drama department at a school is planning a school musical. Activities (duration in weeks; predecessors): A Write script (5; none); B Audition cast (2; A); C Design set and costumes (4; A); D Cast rehearsals (6; B); E Build set and create costumes (3; C); F Rehearse with full staging (4; D, E); G Technical setup (1; E); H Final dress rehearsal (1; F, G).

Identify the critical path and determine the minimum time needed to complete the project.
questions.answer: Path lengths: A–B–D–F–H $=5+2+6+4+1=18$; A–C–E–F–H $=5+4+3+4+1=17$; A–C–E–G–H $=5+4+3+1+1=14$. The longest path is the critical path: A–B–D–F–H, so the minimum completion time is 18 weeks.

questions.question:
The drama department at a school is planning a school musical. Activities (duration in weeks; predecessors): A Write script (5; none); B Audition cast (2; A); C Design set and costumes (4; A); D Cast rehearsals (6; B); E Build set and create costumes (3; C); F Rehearse with full staging (4; D, E); G Technical setup (1; E); H Final dress rehearsal (1; F, G).

What is the float time for Activity E?
questions.answer: E has EST $=5+4=9$ and duration 3. It must finish before F can start at its LST. F's EST is $5+2+6=13$, so E's latest finish is 13 and its LST is $13-3=10$. Float $=\text{LST}-\text{EST}=10-9=1$ week.

questions.question:
The drama department at a school is planning a school musical. Activities (duration in weeks; predecessors): A Write script (5; none); B Audition cast (2; A); C Design set and costumes (4; A); D Cast rehearsals (6; B); E Build set and create costumes (3; C); F Rehearse with full staging (4; D, E); G Technical setup (1; E); H Final dress rehearsal (1; F, G).

Activity C is delayed by 3 weeks, causing a delay to the entire production. By how many weeks is the overall production delayed?
questions.answer: Path A–C–E–F–H has 1 week of float (it takes 17 weeks against the 18-week critical path). A 3-week delay on C makes this path 20 weeks, so the project finishes $20-18=2$ weeks late.

questions.question:
HydroCity relies on a network of water pipes to supply clean water from its main reservoir to three suburbs: Northview, Eastgate and Southbank. Each pipe has a maximum capacity in kilolitres per hour, shown on the diagram.

Calculate the capacity of the cut drawn on the network.
questions.answer: The cut separates the Main Reservoir and $B$ from the rest of the network. The pipes crossing it from the source side to the sink side are Main–$A$ (30), $B$–$C$ (8) and $B$–Southbank (15). Pipe $A$–$B$ flows back across the cut and is not counted. Capacity $=30+8+15=53$ kL/h.

questions.question:
HydroCity relies on a network of water pipes to supply clean water from its main reservoir to three suburbs: Northview, Eastgate and Southbank. Each pipe has a maximum capacity in kilolitres per hour, shown on the diagram.

Determine the maximum flow of the network.
questions.answer: The two pipes leaving the Main Reservoir have capacities 30 and 20, a cut of capacity $30+20=50$ kL/h. The flow can reach 50 (e.g. $A$–Northview 20, $A$–$C$ 10, $B$–Southbank 15, $B$–$C$ 5, $C$–Eastgate 15), so by the max-flow min-cut theorem the maximum flow is 50 kL/h.

questions.question:
HydroCity relies on a network of water pipes to supply clean water from its main reservoir to three suburbs: Northview, Eastgate and Southbank. Each pipe has a maximum capacity in kilolitres per hour, shown on the diagram.

Pipe $BC$ is due for repairs and will undergo a renovation that will increase its capacity. Will the increase in capacity in Pipe $BC$ change the maximum flow of the network? Justify your answer with mathematical reasoning or calculation.
questions.answer: No. The minimum cut is the two pipes leaving the source (capacity $30+20=50$ kL/h), which does not include $BC$. The flow out of the source is already at its maximum, so no extra water can pass through the network, and increasing the capacity of $BC$ does not change the maximum flow of 50 kL/h.

questions.question: A new leisure centre is designed with a running track on its perimeter. The track follows the entire outer edge of the shape shown, which comprises a rectangle and two semicircles. The straight sections are each 90 m. The length of the running track is 400 m. Find the length of the diameter of the semicircles, correct to the nearest whole metre.
questions.answer: The two semicircles form one circle of circumference $\pi d$. $90+90+\pi d=400$, so $\pi d=220$ and $d=\dfrac{220}{\pi}=70.03\approx70$ m.

questions.question: It takes Piper 2 minutes to run around a 400 m track. What was Piper's average speed in kilometres per hour?

The diagram shows the location of three landmarks in a national park: a Ranger Station $R$, a Waterfall $W$ and a Campsite $C$. The Ranger Station is due north of the Waterfall and $\angle RWC=130^\circ$. Isla and Gabriel go on solo hikes from the Waterfall, leaving at 2 pm. Isla arrives at the Ranger Station at 3 pm, travelling at 5 km/h. Gabriel travels directly to the Campsite and arrives at 4 pm, travelling at 7 km/h.

Show that the shortest distance between Isla and Gabriel when they have reached their destinations is 18 km, to the nearest kilometre.
questions.answer: $RW=5\times1=5$ km and $WC=7\times2=14$ km. By the cosine rule in $\triangle RWC$: $RC^2=5^2+14^2-2(5)(14)\cos130^\circ\approx311.0$, so $RC\approx17.6\approx18$ km.

questions.question:
The diagram shows the location of three landmarks in a national park: a Ranger Station $R$, a Waterfall $W$ and a Campsite $C$. The Ranger Station is due north of the Waterfall and $\angle RWC=130^\circ$. Isla and Gabriel go on solo hikes from the Waterfall, leaving at 2 pm. Isla arrives at the Ranger Station at 3 pm, travelling at 5 km/h. Gabriel travels directly to the Campsite and arrives at 4 pm, travelling at 7 km/h. Take $RC=18$ km.

Determine the bearing of the Ranger Station from the Campsite, correct to the nearest degree.
questions.answer: Let $\theta=\angle WRC$. By the sine rule, $\dfrac{\sin\theta}{14}=\dfrac{\sin130^\circ}{18}$, so $\sin\theta=\dfrac{14\sin130^\circ}{18}$ and $\theta\approx36.6^\circ\approx37^\circ$. Since $RW$ is a north–south line, the north line at $C$ is parallel to $RW$, and the alternate angle at $C$ is also $\theta$. The Ranger Station lies north-east of the Campsite, so the bearing is $037^\circ$. (The exact $RC=17.63$ gives $37.5^\circ$, which also rounds to $037^\circ$; using the rounded $RC=18$ with other methods can give slightly different values, e.g. $032^\circ$ or $038^\circ$.)

questions.question: Jenna is designing a logo using two circles with a diamond feature in the middle. The centre of each circle lies on the circumference of the other. Both circles have the same radius of 4 cm. The shaded area (everything inside either circle except the white diamond) needs glitter. Find the shaded area, correct to two decimal places.
questions.answer:
The diamond is made of two equilateral triangles of side 4 cm (the sides are all radii), so each circle has an angle of $60^\circ+60^\circ=120^\circ$ at its centre inside the diamond. Each circle's shaded part is therefore a sector of angle $360^\circ-60^\circ-60^\circ=240^\circ$ (this includes the part of the lens outside the diamond).

Shaded area $=2\times\dfrac{240}{360}\times\pi\times4^2=\dfrac{2\cdot2}{3}\cdot16\pi\approx67.02$ cm$^2$.
